summary: Iteration 36: Tested resource timesheet manual entry (Add Entry dialog + non-allocated project support + over-allocation warning) for riley@test.com. Backend: all 6 pytest cases pass (all-active-summary endpoint, timesheet creation for non-allocated project, project detail access after timesheet). Frontend: Add Entry button, dialog, project dropdown (all 3 active projects), non-allocated warning for Mobile App, and entry creation all work. Submit Week button appears with Draft badge. HOWEVER — over-allocation warning does NOT trigger for Website Redesign because the frontend queries getMyAllocations('week') which uses a 14-day forward-looking window from today (Jul 25, 2026), while Riley's Website Redesign allocation ended Jul 20, 2026. As a result Website Redesign is also incorrectly labeled 'You are not currently allocated to this project'.

ui_bugs.component: MyTimesheets Add Entry Dialog — over-allocation warning
ui_bugs.issue: The `overAllocWarning` computation depends on `allocationForProject` which is derived from `getMyAllocations('week')` (14 days from today, forward-looking). If the resource's allocation for a project ended before today, it is not returned and both (a) 'You are not currently allocated to this project' amber warning shows incorrectly for Website Redesign, and (b) 'You are logging Xh but your allocation is Yh/wk' over-allocation warning never appears. Reproduced with Riley + Website Redesign (allocation 2026-07-10 → 2026-07-20, today 2026-07-25).
ui_bugs.selector: [data-testid="over-alloc-warning"] and 'You are not currently allocated to this project' text

integration_issues.issue: Frontend should either (a) call getMyAllocations without period restriction or with a broader window (e.g., '3months'), or (b) match allocations that overlap the currently-selected timesheet week rather than today+14d. Ideal fix: pass `period='3months'` OR filter myAllocsData allocations whose date range overlaps `currentWeekStart..currentWeekEnd`.

context_for_next_testing_agent: The Add Entry flow works end-to-end for non-allocated projects. The remaining fix is in /app/frontend/src/pages/MyTimesheets.js around line 220-223: change `getMyAllocations('week')` to `getMyAllocations('3months')` (or 'month'). After the fix, re-verify: (1) select Website Redesign → 'not allocated' banner should NOT appear, (2) enter 25 in Actual Hours → over-alloc-warning testid should appear with 'You are logging 25h but your allocation is 20.0h/wk for this project.' — Note: 'today' in the preview env is Jul 25, 2026, so time-window sensitive tests need that context.
rca of the issue: RCA: In /app/frontend/src/pages/MyTimesheets.js line ~222, `getMyAllocations('week')` requests allocations for a 14-day window starting today (period_start=today, period_end=today+13d — see /app/backend/routes/allocations.py lines 729-732). Riley's Website Redesign allocation range is 2026-07-10 → 2026-07-20 but today is 2026-07-25, so the allocation is filtered out server-side (start_date/end_date overlap check fails). Consequently `myAllocsData.allocations` is empty, `allocationForProject` is null for Website Redesign, and both the 'not allocated' banner and the over-allocation warning (which requires a non-null allocationForProject) misbehave. Reproduction: login riley@test.com → /my-timesheets → Add Entry → select Website Redesign. Mitigation: use `getMyAllocations('3months')` or fetch all allocations and filter by date-overlap with the currently-displayed timesheet week rather than today+14d.
